correctness.rationale: For any continuous test function of one coordinate, an antiderivative converts invariance of the flow into the corresponding conditional law. Applying this to the quadratic coordinate energies gives the common cubic-flux identity. If one second moment vanishes, the invariant support lies in the corresponding coordinate plane; vector-field tangency then reduces the remaining coordinates to nonzero exponential equations, whose only trajectory bounded for all positive and negative time is the origin because the relevant parameters are nonzero. Thus every non-origin invariant measure has all three positive second moments and forces the sign condition. Conversely, under that sign condition the displayed squared coordinates are positive and four sign choices give real nonzero equilibria, whose Dirac masses establish sufficiency.
